title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
authors_or_organization: Joel Becker, Nate Rush, Elizabeth Barnes, David Rein (METR)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: METR (non-profit research org); funding details not extracted
limitations: 16 developers, 246 issues, own mature repositories; software engineering, not advisory analysis. Producer-side use of AI (developer is both user and reviewer of AI output), not a client reviewing an outside advisor. Early-2025 tools; authors caution against generalization. 95% CI shown graphically (Fig. 1), not extracted from text.

title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of AI on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality (HBS Working Paper 24-013)
authors_or_organization: Fabrizio Dell'Acqua, Edward McFowland III, Ethan Mollick, Hila Lifshitz-Assaf, Katherine C. Kellogg, Saran Rajendran, Lisa Krayer, Francois Candelon, Karim R. Lakhani
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Conducted with Boston Consulting Group (BCG co-authors); BCG consultants as subjects
limitations: Working paper (not peer reviewed at version accessed). Consultants are the producers using GPT-4, not clients reviewing advisor output; one outside-frontier task designed to trip AI. Correctness judged against a known answer; real advisory tasks rarely have one.

title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
authors_or_organization: Gagan Bansal, Tongshuang Wu, Joyce Zhou, Raymond Fok, Besmira Nushi, Ece Kamar, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Daniel S. Weld
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Authors from University of Washington and Microsoft Research
limitations: Crowdworker lab tasks (sentiment classification, LSAT questions); explanations are model-generated highlights/feature explanations (X2-type), not citations to source evidence (X3). No professional accountability.

title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making
authors_or_organization: Helena Vasconcelos, Matthew Jorke, Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin, Tobias Gerstenberg, Michael S. Bernstein, Ranjay Krishna
publication_date: 2023-04 (Proc. ACM HCI 7, CSCW1, Article 129; arXiv v2 2023-01-26)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Stanford University / University of Washington; funding not extracted
limitations: Online participants on a maze task with a simulated AI; verification cost is manipulated cleanly in a way rarely possible in diligence work. 5 studies, N=731 total.

title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making
authors_or_organization: Zana Bucinca, Maja Barbara Malaya, Krzysztof Z. Gajos
limitations: Lay participants (N=199) on a nutrition/carbohydrate task with simulated AI; full text retrieved but only abstract and summary statistics table reviewed in detail.

title: To Engage or Not to Engage with AI for Critical Judgments: How Professionals Deal with Opacity When Using AI for Medical Diagnosis
authors_or_organization: Sarah Lebovitz, Hila Lifshitz-Assaf, Natalia Levina
data_collection_dates: Ten months of ethnographic observation (over 500 hours); exact years not extracted
limitations: Qualitative ethnography (not an experiment; source_type field approximated) in one US hospital, three radiology departments; AI tools gave no explanations, so it shows effects of opacity but does not test whether adding traceability fixes them. Full text accessed via an NYU Law-hosted copy of the publisher PDF.

title: Overcoming Algorithm Aversion: People Will Use Imperfect Algorithms If They Can (Even Slightly) Modify Them
authors_or_organization: Berkeley J. Dietvorst, Joseph P. Simmons, Cade Massey
limitations: Accessed manuscript version with earlier title; published version may differ. Student-score forecasting by lab (Study 1, N=288) and MTurk participants; no professional accountability or advisor-client relationship.

title: Using Advice from Multiple Sources to Revise and Improve Judgments (discussion-paper version; published as Yaniv & Milyavsky 2007, OBHDP 103:104-120)
authors_or_organization: Ilan Yaniv, Maxim Milyavsky (Hebrew University of Jerusalem)
limitations: Lab estimation tasks (judge-advisor system). The access-to-reasons explanation for egocentric discounting is a proposed mechanism summarized from Yaniv & Kleinberger (2000) and Yaniv (2004), which I did not access directly; not experimentally isolated here. Journal version citation verified via Crossref (DOI 10.1016/j.obhdp.2006.05.006); the discussion-paper text may differ from the published version.

title: The Limits of Transparency: Pitfalls and Potential of Disclosing Conflicts of Interest
authors_or_organization: George Loewenstein, Daylian M. Cain, Sunita Sah
limitations: Short review by the original authors summarizing Cain, Loewenstein & Moore (2005, J. Legal Studies; paywalled, not accessed) and (2011). Disclosure of advisor conflicts is a different construct from evidence traceability (X3) or scope visibility (X4).

title: Accounting for the effects of accountability
authors_or_organization: Jennifer S. Lerner, Philip E. Tetlock
limitations: Only the PubMed abstract (via NCBI E-utilities) was accessed; the review's detailed conditions (e.g., pre- vs post-decisional accountability, known vs unknown audience views) are NOT verified here and must not be cited from this record.

title: Getting comfortable with the numbers: Auditing and the micro-production of macro-order (as summarized in the chapter 'Some critical perspectives on auditing')
authors_or_organization: Brian T. Pentland (original); secondary summary in 'Auditing and Society: Research on Audit Practice and Regulations' (chapter authors not identified on page)
publication_date: 1993-10 (Accounting, Organizations and Society 18(7-8):605-620); secondary summary undated
limitations: Original paywalled (ScienceDirect 403; abstract elided in Crossref/Semantic Scholar). Only a secondary textbook summary was read; page citations to the original (606-608) are the secondary author's, not verified.

title: Mata v. Avianca, Inc., No. 22-cv-1461 (PKC), Opinion and Order on Sanctions (ECF No. 54)
authors_or_organization: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York (Judge P. Kevin Castel)
limitations: Single case with findings of subjective bad faith (continuing to stand by fake cases); not representative of ordinary careless reliance. Shows duty and costs of failure, not the cost of verification.

title: AI Hallucination Cases Database
publication_date: continuously updated; page states last update 2026-11-14
limitations: Counts court/tribunal decisions addressing hallucinated content; maintainer states it does not track the wider universe of fake citations; inclusion involves judgment calls; counts read via a fetch tool summarizing filter counts and may lag.

title: Deloitte to refund government over AI errors
authors_or_organization: Denham Sadler, Information Age (Australian Computer Society)
limitations: Secondary news report quoting DEWR (via AFR) and the updated report. Primary DEWR pages and PDFs (dewr.gov.au) returned 503/connection resets; Finance FOI document also unreachable. Discoverer of errors (reported elsewhere as Dr Chris Rudge, University of Sydney) not named in this article.

title: Government urged to get Deloitte's total fee returned for delivering a botched AI report
limitations: News report of Senate Estimates testimony; Hansard transcript not located/verified. Same underlying event group as WS6-S14.

title: Deloitte breaks silence on N.L. healthcare report
limitations: News report from the outlet that first reported the citation problems; Government of Newfoundland and Labrador primary statements not retrieved (CTV page body not returned). Total number of false citations not given.

title: The hidden costs of workslop
authors_or_organization: Marielle Leon, BetterUp (research credited to BetterUp Labs and Stanford Social Media Lab)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: BetterUp is a commercial coaching/AI vendor with products related to the topic
limitations: Self-reported perceptions; sample size inconsistent within the page (1,004 vs 1,150 US desk workers); no sampling method, weighting, or question wording given; not advisor-client specific. Related HBR article (same evidence group) not accessed.

title: The Tricky Psychology of Holding Government Accountable (interview with Philip Tetlock; republished from The Atlantic)
authors_or_organization: Julie Beck (The Atlantic), republished by Government Executive; interviewee Philip E. Tetlock
limitations: Interview in which the researcher summarizes his own research program; not a primary study; quotes read via a fetch tool's extraction of the page.
